title: Situational Awareness (Leopold Aschenbrenner)
html:
Who: a hedge fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, a former OpenAI researcher. It's named after his June 2024 essay Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead, which argued that artificial general intelligence (AGI) is coming fast and will need enormous amounts of power, data centers and chips.

The thesis: own the "picks and shovels" of AGI. Public holdings included bitcoin miners turned AI data-center hosts (Riot Platforms, Core Scientific, CleanSpark), power (Bloom Energy) and chips and cloud (AMD, Oracle). Private stakes included Anthropic, Fluidstack and MatX.

Timeline

DateEvent
2024–2025Fund launches and grows to roughly $20B in under two years
H1 2026Reportedly +439% net (FT, via Disruption Banking), boosted by borrowed money (leverage)
July 2026AI-stock selloff. With leverage, losses snowball and the fund is forced to sell all its public stocks
Jul 30, 2026Citadel buys most of the stock portfolio at a discount; fund assets fall to about $10B. Anthropic stake kept (TechCrunch)
Aug 1, 2026Aschenbrenner asks investors for new money, calling it one of the best buying opportunities since early 2025
Sep 11, 2026Reported active in options again on AI names. Days later, the new positions were reported underwater (24/7 Wall St. via Yahoo)

Reported peak size and losses vary widely by outlet (figures up to ~$45B peak and ~$35B lost). Treat them as rough.

Lessons for us

  1. Being right on the story isn't enough. The AI build-out thesis may well be correct, but leverage plus concentration meant one sharp drop forced selling at the worst time.
  2. Position sizing is survival. Our Options Playbook caps risk per trade for exactly this reason.
  3. Crowded trades unwind together. This week's chip selloff (hedge funds dumping AI stocks) is the same pattern on a smaller scale.
  4. Someone is on the other side. Citadel profited by buying from a forced seller (see Ken Griffin).
